newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold prices down on strikes, supply rise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold prices down on strikes, supply rise.

text.p: Domestic South Korean gold prices eased this week on soft demand stemming from the recent labour unrest in the country and on an influx of smuggled bullion into the market, dealers in Seoul said on Tuesday.
"The gold price has fallen due to weak demand resulting from the wildcat strikes and the arrival of more smuggled gold," a dealer with Tong Yang Global Corp said.
Gold brought into South Korea through official channels is subject to a three percent import tariff and 10 percent value-added tax on sales.

LG Metals, South Korea's largest gold producer's, daily selling price for gold, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell by 50 won per gramme to 10,070 won on Tuesday from 10,120 won a week ago, a dealer with the company said.
However, LG's silver price edged up to 144 won per gramme, compared with 143 won a week earlier, he added.
Traders said gold's recent fall in the international market to around three year lows, has been offset partially in the local market by the won's depreciation against the dollar.

The won tumbled to 852.90 on Tuesday from 850.10 a week ago. Nationwide strikes, spearheaded by the Federation of Korean Trade Union and the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, erupted on December 26 in protest at the passage of a controversial new labour bill that allows employers to lay-off workers.
